rendered: The room-temperature run was not the proposed separation. It was a comparison. The authors filtered the Cyrene-treated cathode powder at room temperature and at high temperature, then compared the samples by FTIR.[1] The reason for the comparison is that PVDF dissolves in Cyrene only when hot (the DSC data show it dissolved at about 90[2] °C), and it comes back out of solution on cooling.[3] The room-temperature powder still showed the PVDF band, which the authors read as PVDF reprecipitating onto the cathode particles as the mixture cooled.[4][5] The hot-filtered powder lacked that band, which showed that keeping the mixture hot removes the binder. The authors state that controlling temperature was critical because PVDF would precipitate out at low temperature, so the process uses hot filtration or hot centrifugation to separate the foils and black mass.[6][7]
